rule.description: A function defined outside the owner module of struct sc_screen (app/src/screen.c) performs 5 or more direct member accesses rooted at a struct sc_screen pointer and more accesses into struct sc_screen state than into its own module class state, so it primarily manipulates display state that another module owns.

checks.description: Detect non-owner functions whose body reaches into struct sc_screen display state more often than into their own module class state.
checks.detected_relation: function outside app/src/screen.c -> direct member accesses into struct sc_screen (env>=5 and env>own)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The function is more interested in the data owned by the screen class than in the state of the module that hosts it: the behavior belongs with the data-owning class.

matches.evidence: Duplicates the window-to-frame coordinate transformation by reading screen->orientation, screen->content_size, screen->rect and screen->video directly, replicating logic the owner module already exposes.
Computes the virtual-finger position by asserting on screen->window, screen->rect, screen->frame_size and mirroring against screen->frame_size.width/height after delegating the coordinate conversion.
The containment decision for the double-click resize-to-fit path reads screen->rect.x/.y/.w/.h in six comparisons inside the input manager instead of the display class.
The relative-mode gate of the mouse-capture subsystem asserts on screen->mc, screen->window and screen->im.mp and returns the mouse-processor relative_mode flag reached through the screen object.

excluded: Functions defined in app/src/screen.c: owner module of struct sc_screen; accessing its own class state is the ownership baseline, not feature envy.
sc_input_manager_process_mouse_motion: still routes conversion through the owner-side API and composes with a generic helper (2 envied accesses vs 17 own-class accesses, below the rule).

sc_input_manager_process_mouse_button, sc_input_manager_process_touch, sc_input_manager_get_position: rewired call sites whose logic is dominated by their own class state (2, 3 and 1 envied accesses below threshold).
sc_mouse_capture_set_active / sc_mouse_capture_is_active: single window reach-through via mc->screen->window (1 envied access each).
scrcpy.c wiring functions and the app/tests translation units: pointer passing only or outside the production boundary.
